description.narrative: Det övergripande målet för projektet som ambassaden avser stödja är att förbättra skyddet av rättigheter och välbefinnande för HBTQI+-gemenskapen i hela Kosovo
Improve the protection of rights and well being of the LGBTQI+ community across Kosovo

The overall objective of this contribution is: To improve the protection of rights and wellbeing of the LGBTIQ community across Kosovo. Moreover, this contribution will be contributing towards the following specific objectives:
With the support from the Embassy of Sweden, Center for Equality and Liberty in Kosovo will strengthen the institutional capacities, therefore. This will allow the members of the organization and the community to serve its constituencies better and in long term.
Secondly, with this support the Center will provide direct support to members of LGBTIQ persons. The support that the CEL staff offers is very diverse and covers areas of legal support, psychological and professional / academic support. This holistic approach offers a platform for LGBTIQ members to be fully integrated into Kosovo society.
Third specific objective is to work with a wider society, with the aim of raising the awareness of society on principal rights of LGBTIQ community in Kosovo, thus improving societal and institutional protection of LGBTIQ community in Kosovo.
Additionally, it will advocate with key stakeholders in Kosovo in regard to immediate needs of LGBTIQ persons, therefore ensuring policies and budgeting in Kosovo and in the region reflect the needs of this community.

title.narrative: Grant agreement between Sida and Center for Equality and Liberty
Decision on contribution Support to LGBTIQ+ Community (CEL)

description.narrative:
The annual report 2025 from CEL clearly highlights the crucial role played by CEL Kosova in advocating for legal and policy reforms to advance the rights and inclusion of LGBTQI communities in Kosovo. It places particular emphasis on addressing systemic barriers and promoting equality, justice, and non-discrimination.
Mental health support remained a core component of the program. In 2025, five therapists delivered 1,440 psychological support sessions to 93 persons through individualized and communityoriented approaches to address the specific needs of queer individuals. Complementary partnerships with initiatives such as Art Therapy Week, the Prishtina Queer Festival, and Human Rights Week further promoted mental health, visibility, and human rights through creative and educational engagement.
Another achievement was the completion of occupational trainings by 21 individuals, providing marketrelevant skills in fields such as video editing, mixology, social media management, animation, and graphic design. These efforts enhanced employability and professional inclusion, supported by partnerships with allied companies. The program also supported youth development through internships, with two LGBTQI students completing placements at CEL Kosova and gaining practical skills in coordination, communications, and community outreach.
CEL Kosova played a central role in organizing Pride Week 2025, coorganizing the 9th edition alongside key civil society partners. Despite a reduced turnout at the Pride Parade largely due to increased antigender and antiLGBTQI rhetoric, the event successfully maintained visibility, solidarity, and institutional engagement, with participation from highlevel political representatives. Pride Week underscored both the resilience of the movement and the continued need for sustained support.
During 2025, CEL organized a threeday regional conference bringing together approximately 100 participants from across the Balkans. The conference strengthened regional coordination, facilitated strategic dialogue, and produced national and regional advocacy roadmaps, contributing to more coherent and collaborative LGBTQI advocacy efforts at both national and regional levels.
Advocacy efforts delivered concrete results, particularly in combating hate speech during the February 2025 elections. Monitoring and legal action led to multiple sanctions, with three Supreme Court upheld decisions establishing an important legal precedent against hate speech targeting LGBTQI communities.
At the policy level, sustained advocacy contributed to tangible advances, including strengthened protections in the Draft Law on Legal Aid, improved institutional responses to genderbased violence, and continued progress on transgender health care rights and samesex marriage recognition. Together, these outcomes demonstrate lasting, systemic change driven by the project.
The project was implemented through strong internal coordination and close partner collaboration, allowing for timely adjustments. Nevertheless, several challenges were encountered during the reporting period.
Limited transportation support continued to restrict participation by LGBTQI individuals from rural and remote areas, constraining outreach beyond Prishtina. This was partially mitigated through hybrid delivery of trainings, highlighting the need for earlier planning and diversified travel options in future activities.
Anti-gender and antiLGBTQI narratives also affected community mobilization, particularly during Pride Week and the Pride March, leading to reduced participation and heightened safety concerns. Despite this, all planned activities were successfully implemented with enhanced safety measures and increased digital advocacy.
The continued lack of a dedicated space for psychological support services significantly constrained service delivery, especially group therapy. This reinforced the priority of securing a dedicated community space through fundraising and stakeholder engagement while maintaining interim arrangements to ensure continuity of services.
